artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for the VERSION-file dedupe (remedy a), with the release-verify.sh / RELEASE_SETUP.md downstream handoff note

completion_data.completion_summary: Removed the four byte-identical theory_lib/{bimodal,exclusion,imposition,logos}/VERSION files and consolidated per-theory versioning on __init__.py's __version__, relaxing scaffolding and packaging-test requirements before deleting the files so every phase stayed green. A from-scratch build now passes plain check-wheel-contents with exit 0 and no --ignore W002; the full packaging contract suite (including the generate-then-execute journey for all four theories and an independent unpacked-wheel spot-check) is green.

memory_candidates.content: When a packaging lint (check-wheel-contents W002 duplicate-file finding) is caused by files that are asserted as required in multiple contracts (scaffolding REQUIRED_COPY_ITEMS, a conformance test's REQUIRED_ROOT_ITEMS, and packaging-test REQUIRED_ROOT_FILES/_is_data_path allowlists), the safe removal order is: relax every consumer's requirement to optional/absent first (verifying green at each step with the files still present and still shipped), then stop shipping and delete the files last, then verify with a from-scratch rebuild. Reversing this order (deleting first) can break scaffolding paths that read from the installed package (e.g. builder/project.py's REQUIRED_COPY_ITEMS fail-fast) for pip-installed users before the requirement is relaxed.

A risk-closure controlled experiment (build the same wheel twice, once with a candidate file present and once without, then exercise the consuming code path against each unpacked variant) is an effective way to settle whether project-scaffolding code reads from an installed package versus a source checkout, resolving ambiguity that pure code-reading left open.

reflection.what_worked: Following the plan's mandated phase ordering (relax scaffolding, then relax packaging tests, then stop shipping) kept every phase green and independently verifiable, which made the pre-edit-gate probes (grep scope hypotheses, find counts, collected-test-count reconciliation) cheap and conclusive at each boundary.
reflection.what_was_hard: The Phase 7 repo-wide VERSION sweep, scoped to code/ per the plan, still required judgment to classify each hit correctly (deliberately-untouched handoff target vs. an unrelated CLI-flag placeholder vs. this task's own corrected references) rather than mechanically trusting the grep output.
reflection.what_was_missed: The plan named only code/scripts/release-verify.sh as a downstream stale-claim site; the Phase 7 sweep additionally surfaced .github/RELEASE_SETUP.md (outside file_scope, not code/) describing the same now-superseded W002 expectation. It was reported in the summary's handoff note rather than edited, consistent with the pre-edit-gate contract's record-don't-silently-skip rule for an out-of-scope finding.
reflection.successes: All 7 phases closed COMPLETED with a from-scratch build confirming plain check-wheel-contents exits 0 with no --ignore, zero VERSION members in the wheel/sdist, the full packaging contract suite green (106 passed, 4 pre-existing skips), test_generate_then_execute passing for all four theories, and an independent unpacked-wheel spot-check confirming scaffolding still works without the file.
